subject: How to specify SAR (simultaneous autoregressive) process using rgeneric

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: How to specify SAR (simultaneous autoregressive) process using rgeneric
parts:
Hi INLA groups,

INLA provides standard code for CAR process-based random intercept models, whose covariance function for the CAR process reads, [\tau (D - \alpha W)]^{-1}.

I would like to konw is it possible to specify a SAR covariance function for random intercepts e.g., [\tau(I - alpha * W)' * (I - alpha * W)]^{-1}?

Looking forward to hearing from you.
Best wish

vignette("rgeneric", package="INLA")

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to specify SAR (simultaneous autoregressive) process using rgeneric
parts:
Hi Prof. Rue,

I see, but I still have some concerns regarding the reparametrization setting. I list my code below.
Is it possible to spcify the spatial autocorrelation parameter in this way, rho = 1 / (1 + exp(-theta[2L])?

'inla.rgeneric.SAR.model' <- function(
  cmd = c("graph", "Q", "mu", "initial", "log.norm.const",
          "log.prior", "quit"),
  theta = NULL) {
  
  #Internal function
  interpret.theta <- function() {
    return(
      list(prec = exp(theta[1L]),
           rho = 1 / (1 + exp(-theta[2L])))
    )
  }
  
  graph <- function(){
    require(Matrix)
    
    return(Diagonal(nrow(W), x = 1) + W)
  }
  
  Q <- function() {
    require(Matrix)
    
    param <- interpret.theta()
    
    return(param$prec * (Diagonal(nrow(W), x = 1) - param$rho * W)%*% t(Diagonal(nrow(W), x = 1) - param$rho * W))
  }
  
  mu <- function()
  {
    return(numeric(0))
  }
  
  log.norm.const <- function() {
    return(numeric(0))
    
  }
  
  log.prior <- function() {
    param = interpret.theta()
    
    res <- dgamma(param$prec, 1, 5e-05, log = TRUE) + log(param$prec) +
      log(1) + log(param$rho) + log(1 - param$rho) 
    
    return(res)
  }
  
  initial <- function() {
    return(c(0, 0))
  }
  
  quit <- function() {
    return(invisible())
  }
  
  res <- do.call(match.arg(cmd), args = list())
  return(res)
}

Thank

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to specify SAR (simultaneous autoregressive) process using rgeneric
parts:
Hi Prof Rubio,

Thank you for your infomation.
I am not sure whether the above mentioned model can be applied by "slm". Although this model looks like an spatial error model. My model reads:

y \sim binomial (n, p)\\
p = logit(\eta)\\
\eta = \alpha + X\beta + \phi \\
\phi \sim MVN(0,  [\tau (1-\rho*W){(1-\rho*W)}']^{-1})

It should be a GLMM, rather than having a spatial error structure.

Thanks

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to specify SAR (simultaneous autoregressive) process using rgeneric
parts: Hi,

> I am not sure whether the above mentioned model can be applied by "slm". Although this model looks like an spatial error model. My model reads:
>
> y \sim binomial (n, p)\\
> p = logit(\eta)\\
> \eta = \alpha + X\beta + \phi \\
> \phi \sim MVN(0, [\tau (1-\rho*W){(1-\rho*W)}']^{-1})
>
> It should be a GLMM, rather than having a spatial error structure.

I think that this is a ’spatial logit’ model, isn’t it? I believe that you can use the ’slm’ for this too. In the paper that I have pointed out we use a 'spatial probit’, which uses the probit link instead of the logit link. The ’slm’ latent effect is (I - \rho W) ^{-1} (X \beta + epsilon). So, you can get the error term that you want by setting X to a void matrix, so that you get (I - \rho W) ^{-1} epsilon . It works (in the sense that you will get the model fit with no covariates in the ‘slm’ effect) but, as I said, this is still experimental.

Best,

Virgilio
